fix.shows: From the lists of names left off Maharashtra's draft roll for all 288 constituencies, the Sabar Institute counts 2,06,88,421 names, 21.1% of the 9,78,54,049 electors on the roll before the revision, and finds 16.8% of them marked dead. It describes the other 1,72,06,190, marked permanently shifted, untraceable or absent, or already enrolled elsewhere, as alive. It reports that Mumbai's 36 constituencies have 11% of the state's electors and 17% of the names, that in Colaba more names were left off than votes were cast in 2024, and that names left off for a reason other than death exceed the 2024 winning margin in 190 of the 288 seats. It finds 3,250 of the 6,101 third gender electors on the 2024 roll, 53.3%, on the lists. Outside Mumbai, among electors aged 18 to 29 marked permanently shifted, it counts 8,22,798 women and 3,79,991 men, which it reads as consistent with women moving to a husband's home after marriage. The roll has no column for religion, and Sabar classifies the names by religion itself, from the elector's name and the name of the parent or spouse, as a statistical estimate for aggregate figures. By that classification names it counts as Muslim are 14.6% of the names left off, against about 12.1% expected from the 2011 Census. By the same classification, comparing names of the same age in the same seat, the odds of a name it counts as Muslim being marked already enrolled elsewhere, against being marked dead, are 2.07 times those of other names. The report says that name-based matching for duplicates is one possible cause, which the lists do not let it test, and that none of this proves any group was targeted. It finds no difference between the seats of the two alliances once Mumbai, region, reservation, urbanisation and size are allowed for, and the strongest link is with low turnout in 2024. The office of Maharashtra's Chief Electoral Officer replied on 7 November that electors marked dead or already enrolled are a little over 25% of the names and those marked absent or shifted about 75%, that comparing Mumbai and Thane with the state average is not appropriate, and that the revision is still under way, PTI reported.

note: Independent second reading, 8 November 2026: the report's page read through a rendering scrape (dated November 7, 2026, authors Sabir Ahamed, Ashin Chakraborty and Souptik Halder), and the PDF (admin.sabarinstitute.org/api/media/file/SIR_Maharashtra_Preliminary_Report_SABAR.pdf, 305 pages, 993,965 bytes) downloaded with curl and read with pdftotext, pages 1 to 16 in full. Confirmed against the report: 20,688,421 names, 21.1% of 97,854,049, 16.8% marked dead, 17,206,190 others described as alive, Mumbai's 36 seats with 11% of electors and 17% of names, and Colaba's 119,606 names against 118,499 votes in 2024 (1.01 times). Also confirmed: 190 of 288 seats where names left off for a reason other than death exceed the 2024 margin, 3,250 of 6,101 third gender electors (53.3%), 822,798 women and 379,991 men aged 18 to 29 marked permanently shifted outside Mumbai, and the report's reading of marriage. And: Muslim-named electors 14.6% of the names by its own name-based classifier against a census expectation of about 12.1%, the Mantel-Haenszel odds ratio of 2.07 for already enrolled against death within seat and age band, no alliance difference after five controls (minus 0.27 points, p = 0.82), and low 2024 turnout as the strongest predictor (rho minus 0.81). Both quotes are verbatim from the executive summary. The site's figure for Maharashtra is 2,06,88,487 left off the draft, 66 more than Sabar's. The report says its seat totals match the Chief Electoral Officer's table in 287 of 288 seats and that 66 rows in Mumbadevi are missing from the Commission's own PDFs, which is the whole of the difference. The Chief Electoral Officer's reply was checked in PTI's report in Vartha Bharati (https://english.varthabharati.in/india/maharashtra-ceo-says-sir-ongoing-already-enrolled-voters-not-permanently-excluded-2289193, 2026-11-07T23:42:24+05:30), which gives it as a reply to the Sabar survey: a little over 25 per cent dead and already enrolled, about 75 per cent absent or shifted, Mumbai and Thane against the state average, and the exercise still under way. Corrected: the religion figures now say at each step that the classification is Sabar's, made from names as a statistical estimate, as the report says on page 12, and the odds ratio sentence now carries 'by the same classification'. Round 35 carries Sabar's Telangana figures the same way. Sabar's caution follows at once, in the report's words. No conclusion about intent or citizenship is in the site's voice. Earlier reading, 8 November 2026: the first reader's second reading corrected the odds ratio to already enrolled against dead and put Sabar's caution in its own words.
